title: Algebraicity of relative finite Hilbert stacks of an algebraic-space presentation
statement: Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], with universes as in [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $F:\mathcal X\to\mathcal Y$ be a morphism of stacks in groupoids on $(\mathit{Sch}/S)_{fppf}$ [def-pc-fppf-site, def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]: isomorphism presheaves are sheaves and object descent is effective. Suppose $F$ is representable by algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space], meaning that for every $S$-scheme $T$ and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$, $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}h_T$ is an algebraic space $X_y$ over $T$. Assume each $X_y\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Suppose moreover that $\mathcal X$ is equivalent to an algebraic space over $S$ and every $X_y\to T$ is surjective on field-valued point classes [def-trf-algebraic-space-jointly-surjective-family], as a one-member family. Then, for every integer $d\geq1$, the relative finite Hilbert groupoid $\mathcal H_d(F)$ [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids] is an algebraic stack [def-sfb-algebraic-moduli-stack]. No representability of the diagonal of $\mathcal Y$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 06CI (lemma-hilbert-stack-relative-space); finite Hilbert construction in examples-stacks.tex Tag 05WC.

proof.text: Fix $d\geq1$, write $H=\mathcal H_d(F)$ and $H_X=\mathcal H_d(\mathcal X\to h_S)$, and let $q:H\to H_X$ forget $y,\alpha$. Both are fppf stacks by [lem-sfb-finite-hilbert-stack-descent]. The arrow definition [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids] makes $q$ faithful: if two arrows have the same cover map and $x$-isomorphism, compatibility forces their $y$-isomorphisms to agree on $Z$. The positive-degree finite locally free map $Z\to T$ is flat and locally of finite presentation by [def-pc-finite-locally-free]; each fibre has positive dimension as a vector space and hence is nonempty. Thus it is an fppf cover [def-pc-fppf-site], and the fppf sheaf condition on isomorphisms in $\mathcal Y$ makes the two $y$-isomorphisms equal.

Derive the diagonal of $\mathcal Y$ as in Tag 05XW. For $y_1,y_2\in\mathcal Y(T)$ let $I=\operatorname{Isom}_T(y_1,y_2)$, an fppf sheaf. Set $A_i=\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y,y_i}h_T$ and $B=\mathcal X\times_Sh_T$. These are algebraic spaces, and so is $P=A_1\times_BA_2$ [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. They may be viewed as spaces over $T$ by [lem-sfb-space-change-base-to-integers](2). A section of $P$ is a common $(a,t)$ with isomorphisms $\alpha_i:F(a)\simeq y_i|_t$; send it to $\alpha_2\alpha_1^{-1}\in I$. For every scheme $T'\to T$ and $\phi\in I(T')$, the fibre $P\times_Ih_{T'}$ is $A_1\times_Th_{T'}$: $\alpha_1$ determines $\alpha_2=\phi\alpha_1$, and the inverse forgets $\alpha_2$. This identification commutes with restrictions. Its projection to $T'$ is flat, locally finitely presented and surjective by the assumptions on $F$ and [lem-sfb-space-fppf-covering-calculus](2). Therefore [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap], over $T$, makes $I$ an algebraic space. The scheme tests of the diagonal are precisely these isomorphism sheaves (for a pair of objects over the same scheme), so the diagonal is representable.

The morphism $H_X\to\mathcal C_d$ forgetting the map into $\mathcal X$ is representable. Indeed, over a scheme $T$ with cover $Z\to T$, its 2-fibre product is the discrete functor of maps $Z\times_TT'\to\mathcal X$. It is represented by $\operatorname{Res}_{Z/T}(Z\times_S\mathcal X)$ by [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-weil-restriction]; the product is an algebraic space by [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers]. The identification uses the chosen comparison of covers to replace each cover by $Z\times_TT'$; an arrow preserving that comparison and the map into the space is unique. This is natural under pullback by [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids]. Since $\mathcal C_d$ is algebraic by [lem-sfb-finite-cover-stack-algebraic], [lem-sfb-stack-representable-source-algebraic] makes $H_X$ algebraic.

The map $r=(q,p_d):H\to H_X\times_S\mathcal Y$ is representable. To test it, fix a scheme $T$, a degree-$d$ cover $Z\to T$ with $x:Z\to\mathcal X$, and $y\in\mathcal Y(T)$. Step 2 says $E=\operatorname{Isom}_Z(y|_Z,F(x))$ is an algebraic space over $Z$. The fibre of $r$ over these data is $\operatorname{Res}_{Z/T}(E)$, an algebraic space by [lem-sfb-finite-locally-free-weil-restriction]. Explicitly, its object over $T'\to T$ consists of an object of $H(T')$ with identifications of its cover and $x$ with the prescribed pullbacks and of its $y$ with $y|_{T'}$. Transporting along these specified identifications leaves just $\alpha:y|_{Z\times_TT'}\simeq F(x|_{Z\times_TT'})$, equivalently a $Z$-map $Z\times_TT'\to E$. Conversely that map gives the normalized tuple. The normalization isomorphism is specified by the original comparisons; any arrow preserving them is unique. These operations commute with restriction, proving the equivalence of fibred groupoids, not only a bijection on objects [def-sfb-relative-finite-hilbert-groupoids].

Let $T\to H_X$ be any scheme test and put $W=H\times_{H_X}h_T$. As a 2-fibre product of the fppf stacks in step 1, $W$ has descent componentwise: glue the two objects and then the comparison isomorphism using the isomorphism sheaf. An automorphism of an object of $W$ maps to the identity of its fixed $T$-object, so faithfulness of $q$ makes it the identity. Thus each fibre is a setoid. Its presheaf of isomorphism classes is an fppf sheaf: locally equal classes have unique comparison arrows, these arrows satisfy the cocycle condition by uniqueness, and stack descent glues the objects; uniqueness also proves separatedness. The class functor is fully faithful and essentially surjective fibrewise, so it identifies $W$ with this discrete sheaf. These are direct applications of the arrow and 2-fibre-product descriptions [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids] and the stack assertion [lem-sfb-finite-hilbert-stack-descent].

source.place: Tag 06CI, setoid pullback; stacks.tex Tags 05UI and 0432, with the setoid descent argument written out

proof.text: Set $V=W\times_{\mathcal Y}\mathcal X$. The 2-fibre-product formula gives $V\simeq H\times_{H_X\times_S\mathcal Y}(h_T\times_S\mathcal X)$: on both sides the data are $h\in H$, $t\in T$, a comparison $q(h)\simeq t|_{H_X}$, $a\in\mathcal X$, and a comparison $p_d(h)\simeq F(a)$, with the same compatible arrows [def-sfb-stable-pointed-moduli-groupoids]. Since $h_T\times_S\mathcal X$ is an algebraic space [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], step 4 and [lem-sfb-representable-pullback-over-space] make $V$ an algebraic space. For any scheme $T'\to W$, its fibre $V\times_Wh_{T'}$ is $\mathcal X\times_{\mathcal Y}h_{T'}$: the retained object in $\mathcal Y(T')$ is $p_d(h)$. The projection is therefore flat, locally finitely presented and surjective by the assumptions on $F$. Apply [lem-sfb-fppf-space-atlas-bootstrap] to the sheaf $W$ of step 5 and $V\to W$. It makes $W$ an algebraic space. Since $T\to H_X$ was arbitrary, $q$ is representable by algebraic spaces. Step 3 and [lem-sfb-stack-representable-source-algebraic] now show that $H$ is algebraic, as required. At no point was the diagonal of $\mathcal Y$ assumed.
